subject: Engineering Mathematics
summary: a revision of all of Engineering Mathematics: eigenvalues and special matrices, limits, maxima and integration, curl and Green's theorem, first- and second-order ODEs, analytic functions and residues, Newton–Raphson and Gauss–Seidel, and probability distributions

questions.text: For the matrix A with rows (4, −2) and (1, 1), the largest eigenvalue of A³ − 2A is ______
solution: Concept: If Ax = λx, then p(A)x = p(λ)x for any polynomial p: the eigenvalues of p(A) are p(λ).
Characteristic equation λ² − 5λ + 6 = 0 (trace 5, determinant 4 + 2 = 6) → λ = 2, 3
Largest eigenvalue = 21
Exam tip: Never compute A³ explicitly in the exam; work with the eigenvalues.

questions.text: A is a real skew-symmetric matrix of order 5. Then
opts: all eigenvalues of A are real and non-zero
solution: Concept: Aᵀ = −A, so det A = det Aᵀ = det(−A) = (−1)n det A.
For odd n = 5: det A = −det A, hence det A = 0 (B)
The eigenvalues of a real skew-symmetric matrix are zero or purely imaginary (±iβ); with odd order, one eigenvalue must be 0.
Exam tip: The diagonal entries of a skew-symmetric matrix are all zero, so its trace is 0.

questions.text: The value of the limit of (cos x)<sup>1/x²</sup> as x → 0 (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: A 1∞ form: lim fg = elim g(f − 1) (or take logarithms and use L'Hospital's rule).
ln L = lim (ln cos x)/x²; ln cos x ≈ −x²/2 for small x
Exam tip: Memorise cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2 and ln(1 + u) ≈ u; most 1∞ limits fall in one line.

questions.text: The maximum value of f(x) = x e<sup>−x</sup> for x ≥ 0 is
solution: Concept: Stationary point from f′(x) = 0, confirmed by the sign of f″.
f′(x) = e<sup>−x</sup>(1 − x) = 0 → x = 1; f″(1) = e<sup>−1</sup>(1 − 2) < 0, a maximum
Exam tip: 2/e² is f(2), the point of inflection, a common distractor.

questions.text: The value of the integral of x ln x from x = 0 to x = 1 is ______
solution: Concept: Integration by parts with u = ln x, dv = x dx; the lower limit uses x² ln x → 0 as x → 0.
∫ x ln x dx = (x²/2) ln x − ∫ (x²/2)(1/x) dx = (x²/2) ln x − x²/4
Exam tip: In general, ∫₀¹ xn ln x dx = −1/(n + 1)².

questions.text: The curl of the vector field F = yz i + zx j + xy k is
opts: x i + y j + z k
solution: Concept: ∇ × F = (∂Fz/∂y − ∂Fy/∂z) i + (∂Fx/∂z − ∂Fz/∂x) j + (∂Fy/∂x − ∂Fx/∂y) k.
F is conservative: F = ∇(xyz).
Exam tip: Spot a potential first; if F = ∇φ, the curl is zero and line integrals depend only on the end points.

questions.text: Using Green's theorem, the value of the line integral of (x² − y) dx + (x + y²) dy taken anticlockwise around the circle C: x² + y² = 9 shown (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Green's theorem: ∮(P dx + Q dy) = ∬(∂Q/∂x − ∂P/∂y) dA over the enclosed region.
Integral = 2 × area = 2 × 9π = 18π = 56.55
Exam tip: The x² and y² terms contribute nothing; only the 'cross' terms survive.

questions.text: The solution of dy/dx = xy² with y(0) = 1, evaluated at x = 1, is
solution: Concept: Variables separable: dy/y² = x dx.
Exam tip: This solution blows up at x = √2: non-linear ODEs can have finite-escape times.

questions.text: The order and degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0 are
solution: Concept: Order = highest derivative present; degree = power of that highest derivative when the equation is polynomial in its derivatives.
Highest derivative d²y/dx² → order 2; it appears cubed → degree 3: (C)
Exam tip: The power of a lower derivative (here 4 on dy/dx) does not decide the degree.

questions.text: C is the circle |z − 1| = 2 traversed anticlockwise. The value of (1/2πi) times the integral of (z + 2)/[z(z − 4)] around C is ______
solution: Concept: Residue theorem: (1/2πi)∮f dz = sum of residues at the poles inside C.
Poles: z = 0 (distance 1 from the centre 1, inside) and z = 4 (distance 3, outside)
Exam tip: Always check each pole's distance from the centre of the circle, not from the origin.

questions.text: u = e<sup>x</sup> cos y is the real part of an analytic function f(z). A harmonic conjugate v is
solution: Concept: Cauchy–Riemann: vy = ux and vx = −uy.
v<sub>y</sub> = e<sup>x</sup> cos y → v = e<sup>x</sup> sin y + g(x); v<sub>x</sub> = e<sup>x</sup> sin y = −u<sub>y</sub> ✓, so g is constant
v = ex sin y (B), and f(z) = ez
Exam tip: Milne–Thomson: put x = z, y = 0 in f′ = ux − iuy to get f′(z) = ez directly.

questions.text: √10 is computed by the Newton–Raphson method applied to f(x) = x² − 10, starting from x₀ = 3. The first iterate x₁ (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: xn+1 = xn − f(xn)/f′(xn); for square roots this is xn+1 = (xn + 10/xn)/2.
Exam tip: Convergence is quadratic: x₂ = 3.16228 already has 5 correct digits.

questions.text: The Gauss–Seidel iteration for Ax = b is guaranteed to converge for any starting vector when A is
solution: Concept: A sufficient condition for Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel convergence is strict diagonal dominance: |aii| > Σj≠i|aij| in every row.
Hence (A); Gauss–Seidel also converges for symmetric positive-definite matrices.
Exam tip: If the given system is not diagonally dominant, reorder the equations before iterating.

questions.text: Two fair dice are thrown and S is the sum of the numbers shown. The variance of S (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: For independent variables, variances add: Var(X + Y) = Var X + Var Y.
Exam tip: For a discrete uniform on 1…n, Var = (n² − 1)/12; n = 6 gives 35/12.

questions.text: The median of an exponential distribution with rate parameter λ (mean 1/λ) is
solution: Concept: The median m satisfies F(m) = 1 − e−λm = 1/2.
Since the distribution is right-skewed, the median is less than the mean 1/λ, and the mode is 0.
Exam tip: This is the 'half-life' formula of radioactive decay.
